statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: Neutral — 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements may be implicated, but the facts do not show whether a covered financial institution detected the activity and had a reporting obligation.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates that the Secretary require a “financial institution” to report “any suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation of law or regulation,” and provides related protections (e.g., safe harbor and confidentiality) for such reports. Here, the fact pattern describes an entity (SYN_b9c4f88a) conducting several large USD wires and notes “trade-finance over-invoiced,” which could be suspicious and potentially relevant to a violation. However, § 5318(g) applies to reporting obligations of a covered “financial institution,” and the facts do not identify any U.S.-covered financial institution involved, whether the transactions were conducted “by, at, or through” such an institution, whether the institution detected the suspicious activity, or whether a SAR was required/triggered under the Secretary’s implementing rules. Therefore, it cannot be determined from the provided facts whether the conduct described falls within § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements.
